comments.body:
Review remediation (2026-08-21) — narration moved out of the description to keep it under the
plan-review admission limit. What was factually wrong in the original plan and what was corrected,
with file:line evidence.

1. The rule could not be computed where the plan put it.
   `registry.content_triggered_overlays` (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py:416`) takes only
   `(diff_text, repo_root)` and is path-blind by construction — every helper skips the `+++`/`---`
   headers — so the "changes no file under `tests/**`" half of the trigger had no operand there. The
   corrected plan adds a keyword-only `changed_files: Sequence[str] = ()` (existing call sites and
   tests keep working positionally) and passes the step's `changed` list at
   `src/rebar/llm/code_review/workflow_ops.py:99`.

2. The scanned text is not a raw diff. The step receives
   `steps.assemble_diff.outputs.context` (`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml:64`,
   `:118`), i.e. the COMPOSED context: a `## Changed files` list plus orientation plus the diff,
   truncated at `DIFF_CHAR_CAP = 60000` (`assemble.py:30`, `compose_diff_context` `:78-93`). An
   added definition past the cap therefore does not trigger — recorded as a blind spot — and both
   shapes (raw diff and composed context) are now exercised in tests. `changed_files` is unaffected
   by truncation, which is why the negative half of the rule is keyed on it.

3. Gerrit 1547 (`24917e843b`) was miscounted. Its `src/` delta has 0 added `def`/`class` lines and 0
   added branch lines, and it also changed four docs files, so the original "five src-only changes
   all select" acceptance criterion was unsatisfiable. 1547 is now an explicit NEGATIVE case.

4. The corpus shapes were mischaracterised. Gerrit 1920 (`721cb7d6ac`) and 1737 (`1c2bf6e57b`) are
   pure MOVES, and 1703 (`83d91d488c`) is an annotation-only signature rewrite — contradicting the
   plan's claim that "pure renames add no definitions and never trigger". Moves now trigger by
   design; annotation-only rewrites are suppressed explicitly.

5. Rename detection is OFF in the reviewed diff. The gate composes `git diff base...head` with no
   `-M` (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/assemble.py:230`), so a rename reaches the reviewer as delete +
   add. The old `git diff -M` rename-only edge case tested a shape production never sends.

6. Two code citations were wrong: `content_triggered_overlays` is at `registry.py:416`, not `:413`;
   guard (vii) is at `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-tests.md:97` — `:73-75` is the
   Four-Criterion Test bullet, which the plan leaves unchanged.

7. `tests/unit/llm/` does not exist. Both the proposed new test path and the
   `tests/unit/llm/code_review/test_registry*.py` pinning path were unreachable. The flat
   `tests/unit/test_code_review_*.py` layout and the real pinning suites
   (`test_code_review_triggers.py`, `test_code_review_deletion_impact.py`,
   `test_code_review_evals.py`) are named instead.

8. The prompt edit has wider blast radius than stated. Guard (vii) lives in ONE prompt shared by
   Round-A and Round-B, so narrowing it changes blocking eligibility for the whole existing
   glob-triggered population (calibrated at 0.54, "blocks 99 changes / 8.0%"), not only the new
   content-triggered one. That is now stated as intended, with a matching pre-existing-code FP case
   added to the eval corpus.

9. Two consumers were unlisted. `src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml` — the
   calibration corpus the routing `_comment` names, already carrying `R-missing-regression-test` —
   is now in Scope; the `tests`-keyed Pass-4 coach moves (`moves.py:26-31`, `:74-84`), which will
   now offer on ordinary src changes, are recorded as an accepted consequence. Round-A is uncapped
   (`cap: 3` exists only on the Round-B `union` step, `code-review.yaml:118`), so each qualifying
   change costs one extra frontier overlay call.

10. No project overlay could express this trigger. `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` has no `tests`
    entry, and `registry.project_trigger_extensions` (`registry.py:254`) supports only
    literal-substring `trigger_tokens` and additive `applies_to` globs — neither can express "adds a
    definition AND touches no `tests/**`". Hence the committed detector.

comments.body:
Second remediation pass (2026-08-21, worktree at origin/main `960fbfef2f`). All citations
re-verified against that tree and updated — the previous set was computed against an older HEAD and
had drifted (`content_triggered_overlays` is `registry.py:461`, not `:416`;
`glob_triggered_overlays` `:340`, not `:295`; `project_trigger_extensions` `:299`, not `:254`;
`code-review.yaml:63`/`:116`/`:120`, not `:64`/`:118`).

What the rv9 review blocked, and what changed:

1. E1/E6/E2 + A1 — "or a new conditional branch" was undefined and unexercised by any cited corpus
   case. DROPPED. The detector is now added DECLARATIONS only, and the plan says so explicitly with
   the deferral recorded. Every SELECT/NOT-SELECT case in the corpus is a declaration shape, so the
   detector's scope now matches its calibration exactly.

2. T8 — guard (vii)'s "newly introduced vs pre-existing" narrowing gave the reviewer LLM no way to
   decide the distinction: the deterministic trigger signal is used for overlay SELECTION only and
   never reaches the prompt (`workflow_ops.py:61-65` supplies context/changed_files/scope_context).
   Rather than wire provenance through, the plan now specifies the prompt wording in terms the
   reviewer can decide from the diff it already has: newly introduced = implementing lines appear as
   ADDED (`+`) lines in the diff under review; anything reachable only through unadded lines is
   pre-existing and stays advisory; a named violating input = a concrete value/argument/call
   sequence stated verbatim in the finding.

3. project.portability (blocking here) — the earlier draft keyed the detector on `src/**` plus
   Python `def`/`class`, which is a layout-and-language assumption: for a Ruby (`lib/`), Java
   (`src/main/java`), Next.js (`app/`) or .NET target the trigger would silently never fire, and the
   overlay would stay unreachable there with no observable error. Removed both assumptions. The
   detector now reuses the EXISTING polyglot `_REMOVED_DECL_RE` (`registry.py:399-412`, already
   covering Go `func`, Rust `fn`, JS/TS `function`/arrow, `class`) applied to `+` lines, and its
   only path predicates are the committed `tests` globs plus a docs/data extension skip. It is an
   in-process text scan, so no CI provider is involved at all.

Detector design verified empirically before writing it down. The rule is: an added line matching
`_REMOVED_DECL_RE` whose DECLARED NAME is not also removed on a `-` line in the SAME file, and no
changed file under the `tests` globs. Replayed against all five cited commits in this checkout, that
rule reproduces every claimed verdict:
  d9e0f0e733 SELECT (git_adapter.py, 15)   721cb7d6ac SELECT (gitutil.py, 3)
  1c2bf6e57b SELECT (_lib_identity 9 + _lib_mutations 13 = 22)
  83d91d488c no-select   24917e843b no-select
The name-based (not text-based) comparison is load-bearing: 1703 (`83d91d488c`) re-wraps several
signatures across lines while adding annotations, so `+def resolve_event_commit(` does not
line-match the removed one-line signature — only the NAME matches. Counts re-checked directly:
`git show <sha> -- 'src/*' | grep -cE '^\+\s*(async +)?(def|class) '` gives 15 / 3 / 22 / 8 / 0,
matching the plan.

Also corrected: the pinning-suite count. `test_code_review_triggers.py` +
`test_code_review_deletion_impact.py` is 35 tests, not 46 (`test_code_review_evals.py` adds 23, so
58 across all three — that figure was right). Description is 7800 chars, under the 8000 admission
cap.

Implementation pushed as Gerrit change 2090 (commit 62e4245a93f on impl-2e0f, from origin/main 960fbfef2f).

Plan review PASSED (signable, signed at head 960fbfef2f) after two remediation rounds; ticket claimed.

What landed:
- `registry.content_triggered_overlays` gains a keyword-only `changed_files` sequence; `overlay_union` (`workflow_ops.py`) passes the step's changed-file list through and its `description=` now names the added-declaration trigger.
- New `_has_added_declaration` + `_content_selects_tests` helpers: an added line matching the existing polyglot `_REMOVED_DECL_RE`, whose DECLARED NAME the same file does not also remove, with no changed file under the `tests` globs. A separate `_DECL_NAME_RE` does the name extraction (`_REMOVED_DECL_RE` has no capture group) and matches the Go receiver form `func (s *Store) Compute(` by its method name, not its receiver. Anonymous declarations yield no name and are skipped, so the trigger fails closed.
- Path predicates are the committed `tests` globs plus a docs/data extension skip — no `src/**` and no Python-only regex, so it fires for a Ruby, Java, Next.js or .NET target.
- Guard (vii) in `code-review-tests.md` narrowed with diff-decidable definitions; eval corpus gains `R-newbehaviour-named-violating-input` and `FP-preexisting-code-gap-no-new-behaviour`.

Tests: `tests/unit/test_code_review_tests_trigger.py`, 28 cases, all mutation-checked. Eleven mutations each killed a specific test: dropping the removed-name suppression (kills the 1703 replay), never suppressing on a changed test file, dropping the docs/data extension skip, swapping the added/removed buckets, dropping per-file provenance (kills the move replay), removing the trigger entirely, not passing changed_files into the step, weakening the guard-(vii) wording, giving anonymous declarations a synthetic name, blanking the step description, and dropping the Go-receiver alternative.

Gates green in the worktree: make lint, make typecheck, check_complexity_baseline --check (new=0 increased=0), check_criteria_vocabulary, registry.py at 695 lines against the 800 cap, and 412 tests across every tests/unit/test_code_review_*.py plus the vocabulary and prompt-index suites.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
The code-review `tests` overlay (blocking at 0.54 —
`src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json:110-121`) is selected only when a changed file
matches its `applies_to` globs `**/test_*.py`, `**/*_test.py`, `**/tests/**`
(`registry.glob_triggered_overlays`, `registry.py:340-356`). A change adding product logic and no
test file never runs it unless the base reviewer happens to recommend it, and guard (vii)
(`code-review-tests.md:97`) keeps a bare coverage-gap finding advisory.

Four changes adding declarations merged on `LLM-Review +1` with zero test files: Gerrit 388
(`d9e0f0e733`, 15 added `def`/`class` lines, new `git_adapter.py`), 1920 (`721cb7d6ac`, 3), 1737
(`1c2bf6e57b`, 22), 1703 (`83d91d488c`, 8). 388 later produced three bugs (`79c6-eaf3-38af-4ce9` +
two siblings) — the `git_adapter` by-path-load family the epic names. Gerrit 1547 (`24917e843b`) is
a NEGATIVE case: comment-only source delta, 0 added declarations. Approved in the 2026-08-21
fortnight defect review; diff-coverage was rejected — this project tests behaviour, not coverage %.

## Approach
Fire the overlay from the diff CONTENT, where the diff and the changed files are both known.
1. `content_triggered_overlays` (`registry.py:461`) takes `(diff_text, repo_root)` only and is
   path-blind by construction (every helper skips the `+++`/`---` headers), so the "no test file
   changed" half of the rule has no operand there. Add a keyword-only
   `changed_files: Sequence[str] = ()` (call sites stay positional) and pass the step's `changed`
   list at `workflow_ops.py:99`.
2. The detector is a NEW module-level helper (`_has_added_declaration`), NOT extra branches inside
   `content_triggered_overlays`: the complexity ratchet fails on `new>0` and may not be raised. It
   fires when, for some changed file, an ADDED (`+`) line matches
   the EXISTING polyglot `_REMOVED_DECL_RE` (`registry.py:399-412` — Python `def`/`class`, Go
   `func`, Rust `fn`, JS/TS `function`/arrow/`class`) and the NAME it declares is not also removed
   on a `-` line in that same file (per-file provenance from the `diff --git … b/<path>` headers,
   since the composed context interleaves files). `_REMOVED_DECL_RE` has no capture group, so the name comes from a
   SEPARATE regex over the matched line, spanning the same keywords (`def`/`class`/`fn`/`func`/
   `function`, `const`/`let`/`var`). NAMES, not line TEXT: an annotation-only rewrite that re-wraps
   a signature changes every declaration line's text while declaring nothing new. An ANONYMOUS
   declaration (`export default function (`) yields no name, so it cannot take part in the
   comparison and is SKIPPED — failing closed rather than firing on a rewrite; a recorded
   limitation. `tests` is then selected only if NO changed file matches the `tests` globs.
   Added DECLARATIONS only — branch-line ("a new `if`/`for`") detection is explicitly OUT, since
   no cited corpus case needs it; a follow-up may add it with its own case.
3. Portable by construction, not by CI: an in-process pure-text scan, identical under the library,
   CLI and remote-MCP harnesses and under any CI provider or none, assuming NO language and NO
   repository layout — no `src/**` predicate, no Python-only regex — so it fires for a Ruby, Java,
   Next.js or .NET target as for this one. Its only path predicates are the `tests` globs and a
   docs/data extension skip (`.md`/`.rst`/`.txt`/`.json`/`.yaml`/`.yml`/`.toml`/`.cfg`/`.ini`/
   `.lock`), so a fenced code block in a docs-only change cannot fire it.
4. A MOVE is not suppressed: the reviewed diff carries no `-M` (`assemble.py:230`), so a rename
   arrives as delete-in-A + add-in-B whose added names are new to B — 1920 and 1737 trigger.
5. The scanned text is the COMPOSED context: `overlay_union` receives
   `steps.assemble_diff.outputs.context` (`gates/code-review.yaml:63`, `:116`) — a changed-files
   list plus the diff truncated at `DIFF_CHAR_CAP = 60000` (`assemble.py:30`,
   `compose_diff_context:77-92`). Both shapes are tested; a declaration past the cap does not
   trigger (a recorded blind spot), while `changed_files` is truncation-proof — hence keying the
   rule's negative half on it. Accepted consequences: the `tests`-keyed Pass-4 coach moves
   (`moves.py:30`, `:75-82`) now offer on ordinary source changes, and each qualifying change
   costs one extra uncapped Round-A overlay call.
6. Narrow guard (vii) in `code-review-tests.md:97` so a coverage gap is blocking-eligible only when
   the finding concerns *newly introduced behaviour* AND names a *violating input*. No trigger
   provenance reaches the reviewer (`workflow_ops.py:61-65` supplies context/changed_files/
   scope_context only), so the prompt DEFINES both from the diff alone: behaviour is *newly
   introduced* when its implementing lines appear as ADDED (`+`) lines in the diff under review;
   behaviour reachable only through unadded lines is *pre-existing* and stays advisory; a *named
   violating input* is a concrete value, argument or call sequence stated verbatim in the finding
   that the added lines mishandle. ONE prompt serves both rounds, so this also narrows blocking
   eligibility for the existing glob-triggered population (0.54, 8.0% of changes) — intended; the
   corpus gains the pre-existing FP case.

## Scope
Under `src/rebar/llm/code_review/`: `registry.py` (594 lines, cap 800) — `changed_files` kwarg +
`_has_added_declaration`; `workflow_ops.py` — pass `changed` at `:99`, refresh the step
`description=` (`:70-86`); `criteria_routing.json` — `tests` `_comment` only, `applies_to`
unchanged. Also `reviewers/code-review-tests.md` (guard (vii)) and
`eval_specs/code-review-tests.eval.yaml` (one recall + one FP case), both under `src/rebar/llm/`;
new `tests/unit/test_code_review_tests_trigger.py` (`tests/unit/llm/` does not exist).

## Acceptance Criteria
Unless stated: `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_tests_trigger.py -q`.
- [ ] A diff whose only addition is a function/method/class declaration, with no changed test file,
  selects `tests` from `content_triggered_overlays` and, through `overlay_union`, sets
  `include_tests` true — asserted on BOTH a raw diff and its `compose_diff_context` output.
- [ ] Parametrised replay over synthetic diffs of each cited shape: SELECT for `d9e0f0e733` (new
  module, 15 added declarations), `721cb7d6ac` (moved declarations, 3), `1c2bf6e57b` (module split,
  22); DO NOT SELECT for `24917e843b` (comment-only source delta, 0 added declarations) or
  `83d91d488c` (annotation-only rewrite; all 8 added names also removed in the same file). An
  added ANONYMOUS declaration selects nothing.
- [ ] Portability: an added declaration in a non-Python, non-`src/` file — a Go `func` under
  `internal/`, a TS `export function` under `app/`, a Ruby `class` under `lib/` — selects `tests`,
  while a docs-only diff whose markdown fence holds `def f():` and a config-only diff do NOT.
- [ ] A test-file-only diff does not content-select it; a declaration *plus* a `tests/` file still
  selects it by glob (union, not replacement).
- [ ] Guard (vii) defines newly-introduced-vs-pre-existing behaviour and "named violating input"
  in diff-decidable terms, with the Four-Criterion Test bullet unchanged; asserted via
  `prompts.get_prompt("code-review-tests")`.
- [ ] The `overlay_union` step's `description=` names the added-declaration content trigger, not
  deletion-impact as the only one.
- [ ] No regression, no baseline edit: `pytest tests/unit/test_code_review_triggers.py
  tests/unit/test_code_review_deletion_impact.py tests/unit/test_code_review_evals.py
  tests/unit/test_criteria_vocabulary_reviewers.py -q` green with the first two unedited (35 tests),
  `python scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` clean, and `check_complexity_baseline.py --check`
  reporting `new=0 increased=0` with `registry.py` under `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
compiled_state.title: Content-trigger the code-review tests overlay on new src behaviour with no test change
